title: Why does the auction use a restarting countdown?
body_md:
Each bid restarts the lot's countdown instead of letting a fixed timer run out.

In a few sentences, explain what that rule prevents, and name one thing it costs the organisers.
model_answer: A fixed timer rewards sniping: a bid in the last instant wins with nobody able to answer. Restarting the clock means a lot closes only when nobody wants it at that price. The cost is that a lot's length is unbounded, so the schedule cannot be planned to the minute.
